hero.subtitle: AI‑powered IDE & CLI built on the best open source models
hero.description: Open source AI models have caught up to closed alternatives and cost 10x less. Full privacy, native quantization.

home.twoProductsDesc: Whether you prefer a full graphical IDE or a lightning-fast terminal, Edlide has you covered.
home.ideDesc: A full-featured code editor with integrated AI chat, agent mode, and MCP tool support. Built on VS Code for instant familiarity.
home.ideFeature1: AI Chat in the sidebar with multiple models
home.ideFeature2: Agent mode with MCP tool access
home.ideFeature3: Full context window with real-time token counter
home.cliDesc: A powerful command-line AI assistant. Ask questions, generate code, all from your terminal. Open source models.
home.cliFeature1: Interactive chat mode in the terminal
home.cliFeature2: Same models as the IDE: Minimax, GLM, KIMI
home.modelsDesc: Carefully selected and natively quantized. Each model is battle-tested for real coding tasks.
home.modelsFooter: More models added regularly. All models run on decentralized infrastructure.
home.ctaDesc: Download Edlide for free, pick a plan that fits, and get the best open source AI models working for you.

pricing.faq1a: One request is one message to the AI. A simple display-only site uses about 20-30 requests.

pricing.faq3q: Can I change my plan later?
pricing.faq3a: Yes! You can upgrade or downgrade your plan at any time from your Account page. Upgrades are charged immediately (price difference), and downgrades credit the remaining value to future renewals.

pricing.ultraDesc: The ultimate plan for ambitious individual developers.

docs.aboutDesc: Edlide is an AI-powered IDE focused on open source models and privacy. Unlike other AI IDEs, Edlide does not collect or retain your important data, ensuring a secure and private development environment.
docs.openSourceFocusDesc: Work with the best open source AI models without vendor lock-in.
docs.privacyFirstDesc: No data retention - your data stays yours.
docs.installationDesc: Get started by downloading Edlide for your platform.
docs.installationDownloadDesc: Download the appropriate installer for macOS or Windows.
docs.macosDesc: Download the DMG file and install Edlide on your Mac.
docs.windowsDesc: Download the installer and install Edlide on Windows.
docs.accountDesc: Connect your Edlide IDE to your account to access all features.
docs.step1Desc: Navigate to Settings → Account in the IDE.
docs.step2Desc: Click Connect to your account to open the Edlide website.
docs.step3Desc: Sign in or create an account. The IDE will automatically connect.
docs.transferDesc: Import your settings from other IDEs seamlessly.
docs.transferAvailable: Available transfer options in Settings → General:
docs.transferVscode: Transfer from VS Code - Import extensions and settings
docs.transferCursor: Transfer from Cursor - Migrate your Cursor configuration
docs.transferWindsurf: Transfer from Windsurf - Import Windsurf settings
docs.cliDesc: A terminal-based AI coding agent. Same models, same account, works anywhere.
docs.cliInstallDesc: Download and install the CLI from the download page:
docs.cliInstallLinkDesc: Find the CLI install command in the CLI section.
docs.cliConnectDesc: After installation, authenticate with your Edlide account:
docs.cliConnectNote: This opens a browser window where you sign in. The CLI links to your account automatically.
docs.cliStartDesc: Launch the agent in any project directory. Works the same way as Edlide IDE. Same models, same requests quota.
docs.mcpSupportDesc: Supports the MCP format. Same server configurations as in the IDE.
docs.edliderulesDesc: Project-level rules file. Place in your project root. The CLI reads it automatically.
docs.edlideMdDesc: Project memory file. The agent reads and updates it to maintain context across sessions.
docs.availableModelsDesc: Choose from the best open source AI models.
docs.noContextLimitsDesc: Work with large contexts without artificial limitations.
docs.systemPromptDesc: Configure your global communication style and AI behavior in Settings → Rules → System Prompt.
docs.systemPromptNote: The System Prompt applies globally and does not change when opening different projects. Use it to define communication style, explanation depth, and other general AI behavior preferences.
docs.projectRulesDesc: Create project-specific rules for tailored AI responses.
docs.ruleStep1Desc: Click the + button in Settings → Rules.
docs.ruleStep2Desc: Enter a name for your project-specific rule.
docs.ruleStep3Desc: A file is automatically created in your project with a .edliderules extension.
docs.projectRulesNote: Project rules are ideal for specific project requirements that need tailored AI behavior for better results. Each rule applies only to its respective project.
docs.mcpSetupDesc: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers extend Edlide capabilities. First, ensure Node.js is installed.
docs.mcpStep2Desc: Click Add MCP Server to configure your server.
docs.mcpExampleDesc: Add MCP servers by pasting this configuration into your MCP settings:
docs.applySettingsDesc: Configure how the Apply button behaves in Settings → Actions → Apply.
docs.sameAsChatDesc: Use the same AI model for Apply functionality as your chat model.
docs.toolsDesc: Functions that LLMs can call. Some tools require user approval before execution.
docs.autoapproveDesc: Configure automatic approval behaviors in Settings → Actions.
docs.autoApproveEditsDesc: Automatically accepts code edits suggested by the AI without requiring manual confirmation.
docs.autoApproveTerminalDesc: Automatically accepts terminal command executions run by the AI.
docs.autoApproveMcpDesc: Automatically accepts MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool calls made by the AI.
docs.fixLintDesc: Automatically fixes lint errors detected in your code without asking for confirmation.
docs.autoAcceptDesc: Automatically accepts all changes made by the LLM during conversations and edits.
docs.autocompactingDesc: Edlide automatically manages context window efficiency when it reaches 80% capacity.
docs.compactStep1Desc: When context window reaches 80%, the auto-compacting mechanism triggers.
docs.compactStep2Desc: The entire chat session is summarized to preserve key information.
docs.compactStep3Desc: A fresh session opens with the summarized context for better performance.
docs.contextWindowDesc: Monitor your real-time context window usage in the chat interface.
docs.contextWindowNote: Hover over the context window indicator in the chat for 2+ seconds to see your real-time context usage. This helps you understand when auto-compacting will be triggered.
